messages:
tara: FYI — noticing a pretty clear p95/p99 jump in eu-west since the kernel-handoff optimizer landed last night. Traces show more cross-zone routing and longer in-queue times.

mike: Which PR? any quick KV hit-rate deltas? can we get the trace ids + perf dashboard?

perf-bot: Automated summary: 2026-03-16T03:14Z | cluster=eu-west | p95 +120ms, p99 +185ms vs baseline; intercluster routed requests +23%; KV hit rate -4.1% avg (hot prefixes degraded). Top trace ids: 4862a4, 4862b7.

sanjay: I pulled a few samples — looks like continuous-batcher windowing increased effective batch wait for short requests. The kernel selector now prefers the "vectorized_attention_v2" kernel only once batch_size >= 8; but because window_ms moved from 2 -> 6 the short single-token chat paths accumulate and get shipped cross-zone when local GPU is short. That increases serialization and KV cache misses.

emma: quick snippet from the profile where you can see the fallback:
```json
{"req_id":"4862a4","chosen_kernel":"fallback_attention","local_batch":3,"routed":"cross-zone","kv_hit":0.62,"latency_ms":212}
```

liam: My read: two orthogonal regressions 1) window_ms too large for chat-tail workloads -> more batching + routing, 2) kernel thresholding is conservative so we fall back to slower kernel for small local batches. Together they push cost/latency up.

mike: can we test quick mitigations? options: revert window change, lower kernel_batch_threshold from 8->4, or raise locality affinity weight so we avoid cross-zone spilling for short requests.

sanjay: I'll run an A/B canary: adjust window_ms 6->2 for eu-west canary (5% traffic) + kernel threshold 8->4. Also tweak affinity: set locality_weight=0.85 (was 0.6). Expected effect: fewer intercluster routes, KV hit back up, p99 should drop ~100ms.

tara: timeline? impacts to Dedicated customers? any SLA issues?

sanjay: plan: deploy canary in 10m, monitor for 30m, rollback if errors >0.5% or if p99 doesn't improve. I'll also capture KV heatmap pre/post and kernel selection trace.

mike: add a short perf dashboard panel: kernel_choice by local_batch_size + kv_hit_rate by prefix (rolling 5m). put alerts for intercluster_rate > 10% for eu-west.

liam: longer term: we should consider adaptive window_ms based on observed local_batch_size distribution and warm-cache signals (if kv_hit < 0.7, shrink window). This would keep throughput but avoid cross-zone churn.

tara: good. ownership: @sanjay does canary + data capture, @mike will add dashboards/alerts, @liam will draft adaptive-window proposal. I'll coordinate with support if any customer noise appears. :thumbsup:

perf-bot: Canary deployed -> canary_id=c-179500-1 | traffic=5% | start=1795002775. Monitoring panels: p95/p99, intercluster_rate, kv_hit_rate, kernel_choice.

sanjay: (follow-up) I'm seeing kv_hit_rate bounce from 0.64 -> 0.71 in the canary so far, intercluster_rate down ~14%. Will post full heatmaps after 30m.

mike: thanks — please paste the heatmap and a short summary once the 30m window completes.

tara: keeping this thread for status. If numbers look good we can roll the window+threshold tweak to production and then iterate on adaptive-window.
